answer: Proof-of-replication resists sybils: each key seals a private crystal of the canonical sonnet, a fixed public datum, encoded uniquely under that key and bound to its row_txid, so no replica dedups across clones. The seal decays like an ember and refreshes each epoch within a deadline. Because sealing is latency-bound, an operator's fixed device fleet refreshes only so many replicas per close, so doubling live keys more than doubles the hardware needed to meet the deadline. Failure mode: a slack deadline lets one disk reuse idle cycles, reverting cost to linear.
